**Answer: about 29.985 games**

**Setup.** Frank wins each game with probability $p = 0.3$ and Joe with $q = 0.7$. The match ends when someone reaches 21 wins. If Frank wins the match with $j$ losses ($0 \le j \le 20$), the match lasts $21+j$ games, and similarly for Joe.

**Expected value.** Write $P(\text{match length} = 21+j)$ in terms of the negative binomial distribution and use $j\binom{20+j}{j} = 21\binom{20+j}{21}$. Summing the two cases gives

$$E[N] = 21 + 21\left[\frac{q}{p}\,P(\text{NB}_{22,p}\le 19) + \frac{p}{q}\,P(\text{NB}_{22,q}\le 19)\right].$$

A negative binomial tail equals a binomial tail, so with $X \sim \text{Bin}(41, 0.3)$:

- $P(\text{NB}_{22,p}\le 19) = P(X \ge 22) =: A$
- $P(\text{NB}_{22,q}\le 19) = P(X \le 19) =: B$

Since $21\cdot\frac{7}{3} = 49$ and $21\cdot\frac{3}{7} = 9$,

$$E[N] = 21 + 49A + 9B.$$

**Check.** For $p = q = \tfrac12$ and $n=2$ the same formula gives $2.5$, which matches a direct calculation. For $n=21$, $p=\tfrac12$ it gives about $36.8$, matching the known closed form $2n - 2n\binom{2n}{n}/4^n$.

**Numerics.** Let $X \sim \text{Bin}(41, 0.3)$.

- $P(X=21) = \binom{41}{21}(0.3)^{21}(0.7)^{20} \approx 0.0022462$
- $P(X=20) = \tfrac{7}{3}P(X=21) \approx 0.0052411$
- $A = P(X\ge 22) \approx 0.0013130$, summing the tail terms from $P(X=22)$ onward using successive pmf ratios
- $B = 1 - P(X=20) - P(X=21) - A \approx 0.9911997$

Therefore

$$E[N] = 21 + 49(0.0013130) + 9(0.9911997) \approx 21 + 0.06434 + 8.92080 \approx 29.985.$$

ANSWER: ≈ 29.985
